text:
Jack Quinn has finally become the scorer Buffalo drafted eighth overall in 2020. He has 14 goals and 25 points in 25 games, goals in four straight, and a role to match: 18:40 a night, up from 15:39, and on the ice for 81% of the Sabres' power-play time after 37% last season. Our numbers flag him as one of the league's breakouts, and NHL.com now calls him and Tage Thompson Buffalo's "constants."

The scoring is part real, part hot. His own chances are up to 1.18 expected goals per 60 from 0.96, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 54% of his shots coming off the rush last season, so speed is the engine. But he is shooting 19% against 10% last season, and we flag the finishing as due to cool.

The thing to watch is the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.26 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, bottom 2% of forwards, which left him around replacement level overall. This year Buffalo's 5v5 share with him is about even with the team's without him. If the defense holds, the breakout is more than a shooting streak.
headline: Jack Quinn's breakout, and its weak side
